provision deferred tax assets associated with net operating losses generated in various U.S. state jurisdictions. However, with respect to jurisdictions where the Company either has limited operations or statutory limitations on the use of acquired
net operating losses, the ability to utilize such losses is restricted. Therefore, management has determined that a valuation allowance for deferred income tax assets is necessary, as the assets are not expected to be fully realized. The balance of
the valuation allowance associated with U.S. state net operating losses in states where use is restricted for fiscal 2017 and 2016 was $3.2&nbsp;million and $2.7&nbsp;million, respectively. During fiscal 2017, the valuation allowance increased by
$0.5 and during fiscal 2016 the valuation allowance did not change. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">At the end of fiscal 2017, the Company had a $1.3&nbsp;million
deferred tax asset relating to charitable contribution carryovers. These charitable contributions originated in fiscal years 2013 through 2017. Management believes it is more likely than not that the deferred tax asset associated with the charitable
contributions that originated in 2013 through 2017 will not be realized during the carryforward period, which begins to expire in fiscal year 2018. The balance of the valuation allowance associated with charitable contributions whose use will be
restricted due to carryforward limitations for fiscal 2017 and 2016 was $1.3&nbsp;million and $1.3&nbsp;million, respectively. During fiscal 2017 the valuation allowance did not change and during fiscal 2016 the valuation allowance decreased by
$0.1&nbsp;million. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">At the end of fiscal 2017, the Company maintained a $38.6&nbsp;million valuation allowance against its remaining
domestic deferred tax asset; including, but not limited to, the federal net operating loss carryforward and the U.S. state net operating loss carryforwards, whose utilization is not restricted by factors beyond the Company&#146;s control. The
establishment of valuation allowances and development of projected annual effective tax rates requires significant judgment and is impacted by various estimates. Both positive and negative evidence, as well as the objectivity and verifiability of
that evidence, is considered in determining the appropriateness of recording a valuation allowance on deferred tax assets. Although the Company recognized pretax earnings during fiscal 2017, by itself that does not represent sufficient positive
evidence that its deferred tax asset will be realized to warrant the Company removing the valuation allowances established against the U.S. deferred tax assets. Additionally, the Company&#146;s cumulative pretax results for the past 36 months still
remain in a loss position. The Company would be able to remove the valuation allowances in future periods when positive evidence outweighs the negative evidence from the relevant look-back period. However, the actual timing and amount of potential
removal of the valuation allowances currently cannot be reliably estimated. The short-term consequence of being unable to record deferred tax benefits may cause the Company&#146;s effective tax rate to change significantly from period to period. The
balance of the valuation allowance associated with the remaining deferred tax assets whose utilization is not restricted by factors beyond the Company&#146;s control, for fiscal 2017 and 2016 was $38.6&nbsp;million and $46.2&nbsp;million,
respectively. During fiscal 2017 and 2016, the valuation allowance decreased by $7.6&nbsp;million and increased $3.8&nbsp;million, respectively. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Deferred taxes have not been recognized on approximately $79.7&nbsp;million of unremitted earnings of certain foreign subsidiaries of the
Company based on the &#147;indefinite reversal&#148; criteria. No provision is made for income tax that would be payable upon the distribution of earnings, and it is not practicable to determine the amount of the related unrecognized deferred income
tax liability because of the complexity of the hypothetical calculation. </P>
 <p STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="center">F-29 </P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The federal and state income tax provisions do not reflect the tax savings resulting from
deductions associated with the Company&#146;s stock option plans. These savings were $0, $0, and ($0.2) million for fiscal 2017, 2016 and 2015, respectively. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Company or one of its subsidiaries files income tax returns in the U.S. federal jurisdiction, and various states and foreign
jurisdictions. The Company&#146;s U.S. federal income tax returns for fiscal 2011 through 2017 are open tax years. The statute of limitations related to the Company&#146;s 2011, 2012 and 2013 U.S. federal tax years was extended by agreement with the
Internal Revenue Service until June&nbsp;30, 2018. The Company&#146;s state and foreign tax filings are subject to varying statutes of limitations. The Company&#146;s unrecognized state tax benefits are related to state tax returns open from 2006
through 2017, depending on each state&#146;s particular statute of limitation. As of January&nbsp;28, 2017, the examination by the Internal Revenue Service for the Company&#146;s 2011, 2012, and 2013 U.S. federal tax years is still ongoing. The
Company received a Notice of Proposed Adjustment from the Internal Revenue Service which proposed adjustments to taxable income for fiscal 2011, 2012 and 2013 of $6.1&nbsp;million, $5.3&nbsp;million and $6.8&nbsp;million respectively. The Company
has not established uncertain tax position reserves related to this matter as the Company believes its positions will be sustained upon appeal or, if necessary, through litigation. Furthermore, various other state and local income tax returns are
also under examination by taxing authorities. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">As of January&nbsp;30, 2016, the Company had a $1.1&nbsp;million liability recorded for
unrecognized tax benefits, which included interest and penalties of $0.2&nbsp;million. As of January&nbsp;28, 2017, the Company had a $1.2&nbsp;million liability recorded for unrecognized tax benefits, which included interest and penalties of
$0.3&nbsp;million. All of the unrecognized tax benefits, if recognized, would affect the Company&#146;s effective tax rate. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">A

$49.7&nbsp;million and $49.5&nbsp;million at January&nbsp;28, 2017 and January&nbsp;30, 2016, respectively. The fair value of the 7<SUP STYLE="font-size:85%; vertical-align:top">7</SUP>/<SUB STYLE="font-size:85%; vertical-align:bottom">8</SUB>%
senior subordinated notes payable was approximately $50.1&nbsp;million and $49.0&nbsp;million as of January&nbsp;28, 2017 and January&nbsp;30, 2016, respectively, based on quoted market prices. </P>

<TD WIDTH="8%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left"><B>20.</B></TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"><B>Derivative Financial Instrument &#150; Cash Flow Hedges </B></TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Company has a risk
management policy to manage foreign currency risk relating to inventory purchases by its subsidiaries that are denominated in foreign currencies. As such, the Company may employ hedging and derivative strategies to limit the effects of changes in
foreign currency on its operating income and cash flows. The financial impact of these hedging instruments is primarily offset by corresponding changes in the underlying exposures being hedged.&nbsp;The Company achieves this by closely matching the
notional amount, term and conditions of the derivative instrument with the underlying risk being hedged. The Company does not use derivative instruments for trading or speculative purposes. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">For derivatives that will be accounted for as hedging instruments, the Company formally designates and documents at inception the financial
instrument as a hedge of a specific underlying exposure, the risk management objective and the strategy for undertaking the hedge transaction. In addition, the Company will formally assess at least quarterly whether the financial instruments used in
hedging are &#147;highly effective&#148; at </P>
 <p STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="center">F-32 </P>


<p Style='page-break-before:always'>
<HR  SIZE="3" style="COLOR:#999999" WIDTH="100%" ALIGN="CENTER">
<h5 align="left"><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></h5>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">
offsetting changes in cash flows of the related underlying exposures. For purposes of assessing hedge effectiveness, the Company uses the forward method, and assesses effectiveness based on the
changes in both spot and forward points of the hedging instrument. If and when a derivative is no longer expected to be &#147;highly effective,&#148; hedge accounting is discontinued and hedge ineffectiveness, if any, is included in current period
earnings. As of January&nbsp;28, 2017, there was no hedge ineffectiveness. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Company&#146;s United Kingdom subsidiary is exposed to
foreign currency risk from inventory purchases. In order to mitigate the financial risk of settlement of inventory at various prices based on movement of the U.S. dollar against the British pound, the Company entered into foreign currency forward
exchange contracts (the &#147;Hedging Instruments&#148;). These are formally designated and &#147;highly effective&#148; as cash flow hedges. The Company will hedge approximately 45% of its U.S. dollar denominated purchases. All changes in the
Hedging Instruments&#146; fair value associated with inventory purchases are recorded in equity as a component of accumulated other comprehensive income until the underlying hedged item is reclassified to earnings. The Company records the foreign
currency forward exchange contracts at fair value in its Consolidated Balance Sheets. The cash flows from derivative instruments that are designated as cash flow hedges are classified in the same category as the cash flows from the underlying hedged
items. In the event that hedge accounting is discontinued, cash flows subsequent to the date of discontinuance are classified within investing activities.&nbsp;The Company considers the classification of the underlying hedged item&#146;s cash flows
in determining the classification for the designated derivative instrument&#146;s cash flows. The Company classifies derivative instrument cash flows from hedges of foreign currency risk on the settlement of inventory as operating activities. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Company&#146;s Hedging Instruments were classified within Level&nbsp;2 of the fair value hierarchy. The following table summarizes the
effects, fair value and balance sheet classification of the Company&#146;s Hedging Instruments. </P> <P STYLE="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>

<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"><B>Related Party Transactions </B></TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Company leases approximately 16,000 square feet for
administrative offices, and leased approximately 50,000 square feet for warehouse distribution and retail, at facilities owned by its Executive Chairman of the Board, George Feldenkreis. These facilities were designed specifically for use by the
Company and were originally leased by the Company under a <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">10-year</FONT> lease for the office space and a <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">10-year</FONT> lease for the warehouse and retail space. These facilities are
in close proximity to the Company&#146;s Miami, Florida headquarters. During the first half of fiscal 2015, the Company amended the leases to extend the term for five years, beginning July&nbsp;1, 2014 and expiring June&nbsp;30, 2019. Pursuant to
those amendments, beginning July&nbsp;1, 2014, the basic monthly rent became $41,750 and increases 3% on the first month of each of the remaining <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">12-month</FONT> periods during the extended term. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Rent expense, including insurance and taxes, for these leases amounted to approximately $487,000, or $9.87 per square foot, and $610,000, or
$9.25 per square foot, for the years ended, January&nbsp;30, 2016,&nbsp;and January&nbsp;31, 2015, respectively. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">As of October&nbsp;1,
2014, the Company transitioned its operations out of the warehouse space. In order to minimize the costs associated with an early termination of the lease relating to the warehouse and retail space, the Company engaged a real estate broker to assist
it in finding a replacement tenant and agreed to be responsible for the related brokerage fees incurred of approximately $215,000. The retained broker identified a new tenant for the warehouse and retail space that is unrelated to the Company. The
Company entered into a lease termination agreement relating to the warehouse and retail space on April&nbsp;13, 2015. The Company incurred $180,000 of lease termination fees, including costs related to certain tenant improvements such as painting
the interior and exterior of the building and improvements to the parking lot, which were agreed upon in order to induce the new tenant to lease the space and allow the Company to terminate the lease prior to its expiration. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Because of the termination of the warehouse and retail lease, the basic monthly rent has been reduced to $14,666 and will increase 3% on the
first of each of the remaining <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">12-month</FONT> periods during the extended term. Rent expense, including insurance and taxes, for the updated lease amounted to approximately $243,000, or $15.19 per square foot, for
the year ended January&nbsp;28, 2017. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">During the years ended January&nbsp;30, 2016 and January&nbsp;31, 2015, the Company chartered an
aircraft from a third party aircraft charter business, who chartered the aircraft from an entity controlled by the Executive Chairman and the Chief Executive Officer. The Company paid $42,000 and $1.6&nbsp;million for flights related to the aircraft
owned by Executive Chairman and the Chief Executive Officer for the years ended January&nbsp;30, 2016 and January&nbsp;31, 2015, respectively. There were no payments made in fiscal 2017. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Company is a party to licensing agreements with Isaco International, Inc. (&#147;Isaco&#148;), pursuant to which Isaco has been granted
the exclusive license to use various Perry Ellis trademarks in the United States and Puerto Rico to market a line of men&#146;s underwear, hosiery and loungewear. The principal shareholder of Isaco is the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap"><FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">father-in-law</FONT></FONT> of the Company&#146;s President and Chief Executive Officer. Royalty income earned from the Isaco license agreements amounted to approximately $2.2&nbsp;million, $2.1&nbsp;million and
$2.3&nbsp;million for the years ended January&nbsp;28, 2017, January&nbsp;30, 2016,&nbsp;and January&nbsp;31, 2015, respectively. Advertising reimbursements from the Isaco license agreements amounted to approximately $0.5&nbsp;million for each of
the years ended January&nbsp;28, 2017, January&nbsp;30, 2016,&nbsp;and January&nbsp;31, 2015. In addition, the Company has purchased product from Isaco for sales in its
<FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap"><FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">direct-to-consumer</FONT></FONT> business. Total product purchased amounted to approximately $0.6&nbsp;million, $0.7&nbsp;million and $0.8&nbsp;million for the years ended
January&nbsp;28, 2017, January&nbsp;30, 2016,&nbsp;and January&nbsp;31, 2015, respectively. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Company is a party to an agreement with
Sprezzatura Insurance Group LLC. Joseph Hanono, the nephew of the Company&#146;s Chief Executive Officer, is a member of Sprezzatura Insurance Group. The Company paid under this agreement, to this third party $0.8&nbsp;million $0.9&nbsp;million and
$1.0&nbsp;million in premiums for property and casualty insurance for the years ended January&nbsp;28, 2017, January&nbsp;30, 2016,&nbsp;and January&nbsp;31, 2015, respectively. </P>

<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"><B>Stock Options, SARS and Restricted Shares </B></TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">In 2005, the Company adopted the 2005
Long-Term Incentive Compensation Plan (the &#147;2005 Plan&#148;). The 2005 Plan allowed the Company to grant options and other awards to purchase or receive up to an aggregate of 2,250,000 shares of the Company&#146;s common stock, reduced by any
awards outstanding under the 2002 Plan. On March&nbsp;13, 2008, the Board of Directors unanimously adopted an amendment and restatement of the 2005 Plan that increased the number of shares available for grants to an aggregate of 4,750,000 shares of
common stock. On March&nbsp;17, 2011, the Board of Directors unanimously adopted the second amendment and restatement of the 2005 Plan, which increased the number of shares available for grants by an additional 500,000 shares to an aggregate of
5,250,000 shares of common stock. On May&nbsp;20, 2015, the Board of Directors unanimously adopted, subject to shareholder approval at the annual meeting, the Perry Ellis International, Inc. 2015 Long Term Incentive Compensation Plan, which is an
amendment and restatement of the 2005 Plan (the &#147;2015 Plan, and collectively with the 2002 Plan and the prior 2005 Plan, as amended, the &#147;Stock Plans&#148;). The amendment was approved by the shareholders at the Company&#146;s 2015 annual
meeting. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The 2015 Plan extends the term of the 2005 Plan until July&nbsp;17, 2025 as well as increases the number of shares of common
stock reserved for issuance by an additional 1,000,000 shares to an aggregate of 6,250,000 shares. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Stock Plans are designed to serve
as an incentive for attracting and retaining qualified and competent employees, officers, directors, consultants, and other persons who provide services to the Company. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The 2015 Plan provides for grants of, among other securities, restricted stock, stock appreciation rights or SARS, Incentive Stock Options and
Nonstatutory Stock Options. An Incentive Stock Option is an option to purchase common stock, which meets the requirements set forth under Section&nbsp;422 of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended (&#147;Section&nbsp;422&#148;). A
Nonstatutory Stock Option is an option to purchase common stock, which meets the requirements of the 2015 Plan, but does not meet the definition of an &#147;incentive stock option&#148; under Section&nbsp;422. </P>
 <p STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="center">F-35 </P>

approximately $0.1&nbsp;million. This value is being recorded as compensation expense on a straight-line basis over the vesting period of each SAR. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">During fiscal 2015, the Company granted SARS to purchase shares of common stock to certain key employees. The Company awarded an aggregate of
3,501 SARS with an exercise price of $20.12, which generally vest over a three-year period and have a seven-year term. The total fair value of the SARS, based on the Black-Scholes Option Pricing Model, amounted to approximately $38,000, which is
being recorded as compensation expense on a straight-line basis over the vesting period of each SAR. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Also, during fiscal 2015, the
Company granted an aggregate of 5,883, 5,157 and 3,816 SARs, to be settled in shares of common stock, to three directors, respectively. The SARs have an exercise price of $15.49, $17.71 and $24.26, respectively, generally vest over a three-year
period and have a seven-year term. The total fair value of the SARs, based on the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Black-Scholes</FONT> Option Pricing Model, amounted to approximately $50,000, $50,000 and $50,000 respectively, which is being
recorded as compensation expense on a straight-line basis over the vesting period of each SAR. </P>

</TABLE> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><I>Restricted Stock</I> &#150; Under the 2015 Plan, restricted stock awards are granted subject to
restrictions on transferability, risk of forfeiture and other restrictions, if any, as the Committee may impose, or as otherwise provided in the 2015 Plan, covering a period of time specified by the Committee. The terms of any restricted stock
awards granted under the 2015 Plan are set forth in a written Award Agreement, which contains provisions determined by the Committee and not inconsistent with the 2015 Plan. The restrictions may lapse separately or in combination at such times,
under such circumstances (including based on achievement of performance goals and/or future service requirements), in such installments or otherwise, as the Committee may determine at the date of grant or thereafter. Except to the extent restricted
under the terms of the 2005 Plan and any Award Agreement relating to a restricted stock award, a participant granted restricted stock shall have all of the rights of a shareholder, including the right to vote the restricted stock and the right to
receive dividends thereon (subject to any mandatory reinvestment or other requirement imposed by the Committee). During the Restriction Period (as defined in the 2005 Plan), the restricted stock may not be sold, transferred, pledged, hypothecated,
margined or otherwise encumbered by the participant. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">During fiscal 2017, the Company granted an aggregate of 115,588 shares of restricted
stock to certain key employees, which vest primarily over a three-year period, at an estimated value of $2.2&nbsp;million. This value is being recorded as compensation expense on a straight-line basis over the vesting period of the restricted stock.
</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Also, during fiscal 2017, the Company awarded to six directors an aggregate of 31,902 shares of restricted stock. The restricted stock
awarded vests over a <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">one-year</FONT> period, at an estimated value of $0.7&nbsp;million. This value is being recorded as compensation expense on a straight-line basis over the vesting period of the restricted stock.
</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">During fiscal 2017, the Company granted performance-based restricted stock to certain key employees. Such stock vests 100% in April 2019,
provided that each employee is still an employee of the Company on such date, and that the Company has met certain performance criteria.&nbsp;A total of 184,004 shares of performance-based restricted stock were issued at an estimated value of
$3.5&nbsp;million. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">During fiscal 2017, of the 337,685 restricted shares that vested, a total of 171,871 shares had 49,387 shares were
withheld to cover the employees&#146; minimum statutory income tax requirements. The estimated value of the withheld shares was $1.0&nbsp;million. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">During fiscal 2016, the Company granted an aggregate of 219,566 shares of restricted stock to certain key employees, which vest primarily over
a three-year period, at an estimated value of $5.4&nbsp;million. This value is being recorded as compensation expense on a straight-line basis over the vesting period of the restricted stock. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Also, during fiscal 2016, the Company awarded to five directors an aggregate of 12,840 shares of restricted stock. The restricted stock
awarded vests primarily over a three-year period, at an estimated value of $0.3&nbsp;million. This value is being recorded as compensation expense on a straight-line basis over the vesting period of the restricted stock. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">During fiscal 2016, of the 242,968 restricted shares that vested, a total of 91,083 shares had 27,325 shares were withheld to cover the
employees&#146; minimum statutory income tax requirements. The estimated value of the withheld shares was $0.7&nbsp;million. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">During
fiscal 2015, the Company granted an aggregate of 255,390 shares of restricted stock to certain key employees, with an estimated value of $3.8&nbsp;million, which vest over a three to five year period. </P>

<TD WIDTH="8%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left"><B>24.</B></TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"><B>Segment Information </B></TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Company has four reportable segments: Men&#146;s Sportswear and
Swim, Women&#146;s Sportswear, <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap"><FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Direct-to-Consumer</FONT></FONT> and Licensing. The Men&#146;s Sportswear and Swim and Women&#146;s Sportswear segments derive revenues from the design,
import and distribution of apparel to department stores and other retail outlets, principally throughout the United <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap"><FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">States.&nbsp;The&nbsp;Direct-to-Consumer</FONT></FONT> segment
derives its revenues from the sale of the Company&#146;s branded and licensed products through the Company&#146;s retail stores and <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">e-commerce</FONT> platforms. The Licensing segment derives its revenues from
royalties associated from the use of the Company&#146;s brand names, principally Perry Ellis, Original Penguin, Laundry, Gotcha, Pro Player, Farah, Ben Hogan and John Henry. See footnote 2 to the consolidated financial statements for disclosure of
major customers. </P>

16,000 square feet for administrative offices, from its Chairman. During fiscal 2015, the Company amended the lease to extend the term for 60 months, beginning July&nbsp;1, 2014 and expiring June&nbsp;30, 2019. Beginning July&nbsp;1, 2014, the basic
monthly rent was $14,666, which increases 3% on the first of each of the remaining <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">12-month</FONT> periods during the extended term. </P>

<h5 align="left"><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></h5>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Company leases several locations for offices, showrooms and retail stores primarily
throughout the United States. Lease terms generally range from approximately 3 to 15 years, including anticipated renewal options. The leases generally provide for minimum annual rental payments and are subject to escalations based upon increases in
the consumer price index, contractual base rent increases, real estate taxes and other costs. In addition, certain leases contain contingent rental provisions based upon the sales of the underlying retail stores. Certain leases also provide for rent
deferral during the initial term of such lease, landlord contributions, and/or scheduled minimum rent increases during the terms of the leases. These leases are classified as either capital leases or operating leases as appropriate. For financial
reporting purposes, rent expense associated with operating leases is recorded on a straight-line basis over the life of the lease. These leases expire through 2028. Minimum aggregate annual commitments for the Company&#146;s <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-cancelable,</FONT> unrelated operating lease commitments are as follows: </P> <P STYLE="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
